narrative.explanation: Rebuilding the P&L from the movement columns reaches RON 5,843,449.04; statutory profit in account 121 is RON 1,435,533.59. The unexplained step of RON -4,407,915.45 is 75.4% of the RON 5,843,449.04 it is bridging. Graded critical: the amount at stake is 75.4% of reconstructed net income, against the ladder printed beside this finding. The step is graded against the profit it is correcting. A bridge worth a tenth of the answer is a footnote; one worth half of it means the reconstruction is not the source of the printed profit.

narrative.explanation: 38.5% of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of RON 94,519,044.80 carries 25.6 years of life at the current annual charge of RON 3,695,525.59. Graded low: the amount at stake is 38.5% of gross pp&e, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Depreciation is graded against the asset base that produced it, so a factory and a courier are compared on the share of their OWN gross PP&E already written off rather than on an absolute charge.

narrative.so_what: Ask for the fixed-asset register by acquisition year and the committed capex plan. A book this far through its depreciation life either has replacement spending ahead of it or is running assets past their useful life, and the two have very different cash consequences.

insights.claim: The net trade float is RON -2,192,704.48: RON 10,829,721.07 owed by customers against RON 13,022,425.55 owed to suppliers — 39.8 days of sales outstanding against 82.8 days of payables, a gap of -43.0 days.
insights.claim_template: The net trade float is {money:float}: {money:trade_receivables} owed by customers against {money:trade_payables} owed to suppliers — {measure:dso} of sales outstanding against {measure:dpo} of payables, a gap of {measure:float_days}.
insights.formula: DSO = trade receivables net ÷ revenue × 365; DPO = trade payables ÷ cost of goods sold × 365; float = trade receivables net − trade payables

narrative.explanation: The net trade float is RON -2,192,704.48: RON 10,829,721.07 owed by customers against RON 13,022,425.55 owed to suppliers — 39.8 days of sales outstanding against 82.8 days of payables, a gap of -43.0 days. Graded low: the amount at stake is 2.2% of revenue, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Trade float is a claim on a year of trading, so it is graded as a share of that year's revenue — the same base both day counts already annualise against.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Compare the collection gap with the credit terms actually granted. Where suppliers fund the cycle, that funding is a payables line that can be withdrawn, not a permanent source.
